ac2.command:
set -u
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ac2 RED: python3 missing - the amendment reconstruction cannot run"; exit 1; }
A=docs/state/outputs/t123_definer_gate_amendment.json
test -f "$A" || { echo "ac2 RED: $A missing - the leg-288 amendment record is the measured bridge between the old fence and the new one"; exit 1; }
D=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$D"' EXIT
python3 - "$A" "$D" <<'PYEOF' || exit 1
import hashlib, json, sys
rec = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
d = sys.argv[2]
tests = json.load(open("docs/state/merge_test_index.json", encoding="utf-8"))["tests"]
am = [a for a in rec["amendments"] if a["index"] == 288][0]
live = tests[288]["command"]
regions = am["replaced_regions"]
def csha(s): return hashlib.sha256(s.encode()).hexdigest()
def esha(x): return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(x, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
if csha(live) == am["old_command_sha256"] and len(live) == am["old_command_len"] and esha(tests[288]) == am["entry_sha_before"]:
    for r in regions:
        if live.count(r["from"]) != 1:
            print("ac2 RED: region from-string not unique in the live command: %r" % r["from"][:60]); sys.exit(1)
    old_cmd = live
    new_cmd = live
    for r in regions:
        new_cmd = new_cmd.replace(r["from"], r["to"], 1)
    if csha(new_cmd) != am["new_command_sha256"] or len(new_cmd) != am["new_command_len"]:
        print("ac2 RED: the regions do not reconstruct the amended command the record pins"); sys.exit(1)
    base = "pre-merge (the live index still carries the OLD leg-288 command; the W2 proposal is unapplied)"
elif csha(live) == am["new_command_sha256"] and esha(tests[288]) == am["entry_sha_after"]:
    new_cmd = live
    old_cmd = live
    for r in reversed(regions):
        old_cmd = old_cmd.replace(r["to"], r["from"], 1)
    if csha(old_cmd) != am["old_command_sha256"]:
        print("ac2 RED: reverse reconstruction of the OLD command failed after apply"); sys.exit(1)
    base = "post-apply (the orchestrator has applied the W2 amendment; the live entry IS the amended command)"
else:
    print("ac2 RED: leg 288 matches neither the old nor the amended pins - the index moved off both bases; re-pin before applying")
    sys.exit(1)
open(d + "/old_cmd.sh", "w", newline="\n").write(old_cmd + "\n")
open(d + "/new_cmd.sh", "w", newline="\n").write(new_cmd + "\n")
sys.stdout.write("ac2 evidence: both leg-288 command variants materialised from the amendment record against the live index - %s\n" % base)
PYEOF
rc_old=0; bash "$D/old_cmd.sh" >"$D/old.out" 2>&1 || rc_old=$?
rc_new=0; bash "$D/new_cmd.sh" >"$D/new.out" 2>&1 || rc_new=$?
if [ "$rc_old" -eq 0 ] && [ "$rc_new" -eq 1 ]; then
  if grep -q "safe_local_remediation" "$D/new.out"; then
    echo "ac2 evidence: measured at the pre-merge tree - the OLD two-class fence is GREEN and the NEW three-class fence is RED naming the third class; the builder must land the class (the groom-time state, disclosed not hidden)"
    echo "ac2 GREEN: leg 288 flips exactly with the product - both fences reconstruct from the record and the pair is live at this tree"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "ac2 RED: the new fence went RED but not for the third-class reason - outputs follow"; tail -5 "$D/new.out"; exit 1
fi
if [ "$rc_old" -eq 1 ] && [ "$rc_new" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "ac2 evidence: measured on the product tree - the OLD fence is RED (necessity: it refuses the third class) and the AMENDED fence is GREEN (sufficiency: exactly three scoped classes, six negative controls armed)"
  echo "ac2 GREEN: leg 288 flips exactly with the product - old fence RED on the third class, amended fence GREEN on three scoped classes and RED again on any drift either way"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$rc_old" -eq 0 ] && [ "$rc_new" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "ac2 RED: BOTH fences are GREEN on this tree - the amended probe is a relaxation, not a re-premise (it must REFUSE the two-class state)"; exit 1
fi
echo "ac2 RED: unexpected rc pair old=$rc_old new=$rc_new - outputs follow"; tail -5 "$D/old.out"; tail -5 "$D/new.out"; exit 1
